issues.description: The phrase Bạn trông ốm quá is understandable, but in everyday Southern Vietnamese it can also sound like a comment about weight, and it feels a little translated. A clearer, more natural phrase for a friend who looks unwell would be Bạn trông không khỏe.
issues.suggested_fix: Bạn trông không khỏe, Ben. Có chuyện gì vậy?

issues.description: Bạn không nên đi làm hôm nay is clear, but the time expression sounds slightly English-influenced. In spoken Vietnamese, it is more natural to put hôm nay earlier.
issues.suggested_fix: Bạn nên đến hiệu thuốc. Hôm nay bạn không nên đi làm.

issues.description: The gloss for headache says when your head feels bad. At A2, I would understand it, but hurts is simpler and closer to đau đầu. The Vietnamese gloss could also include the common phrase used in the dialogue.
issues.suggested_fix: headache: en when your head hurts; vi đau đầu; cơn đau đầu

qa_report.summary: The clip is short, clear, and suitable for A2. I can follow the problem, the advice, and the grammar point with should and shouldn't. The Vietnamese is mostly good, with only small naturalness and gloss improvements.
